# Overview

The **chirps** package provides access to climate datasets produced by the Climate Hazards Center (CHC), University of California Santa Barbara. Data are read directly from the CHC server. The package returns time series for points and polygons, or the original raster products through the **terra** package.

| Dataset             | Variables                   | Coverage     | Period                         |
| ------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------ |
| CHIRPS v3 (default) | Precipitation               | 60°S to 60°N | 1981 to near present           |
| CHIRPS v2           | Precipitation               | 50°S to 50°N | 1981 to December 2026 (retired) |
| CHIRTS-daily        | Tmax, Tmin, RHum, HeatIndex | 60°S to 70°N | 1983 to 2016                   |
| CHIRTS-ERA5         | Tmax, Tmin                  | 60°S to 70°N | 1980 to near present           |

Climate indices are out of scope for **chirps**. The [climatrends](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=climatrends) package computes rainfall, temperature, growing degree days, evapotranspiration and crop sensitive indices, and it takes the output of **chirps** directly.

## Time series for points

`get_chirps()` returns one row per location and day, ordered by `id` and `date`.

```r
library("chirps")

lonlat = data.frame(lon = c(-55.0281, -54.9857, -55.0714),
                    lat = c(-2.8094, -2.8756, -3.5279))

dates = c("2017-01-01", "2017-01-31")

dat = get_chirps(lonlat, dates)

head(dat)
```

A single date returns one day.

```r
day1 = get_chirps(lonlat, "2017-01-15")
```

CHIRPS v3 has two daily products. `type = "rnl"` (default) splits the pentadal totals into days with ERA5, and `type = "sat"` uses NASA IMERG.

```r
dat_sat = get_chirps(lonlat, dates, type = "sat")
```

## Time series for polygons

With `sf` or `SpatVector` polygons, each day is summarised over the cells that touch each polygon. The average is the default, and `operation` sets another summary (0 max, 1 min, 2 median, 4 sum, 5 average).

```r
data("tapajos", package = "chirps")

rain_mean = get_chirps(tapajos, dates)

rain_total = get_chirps(tapajos, dates, operation = 4)
```

## Temperature

`get_chirts()` works the same way for temperature. CHIRTS-daily covers 1983 to 2016. For other years, use `product = "CHIRTS-ERA5"`, which covers maximum and minimum temperature from 1980 to near present.

```r
tmax = get_chirts(lonlat, c("2010-01-01", "2010-01-31"), var = "Tmax")

tmin = get_chirts(lonlat, c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31"), var = "Tmin",
                  product = "CHIRTS-ERA5")
```

## Climate indices with climatrends

With `as.matrix = TRUE`, **chirps** returns one row per location and one column per day, named "YYYY-MM-DD". This is the input that climatrends expects.

```r
library("climatrends")

rain = get_chirps(lonlat, dates, as.matrix = TRUE)

rainfall(rain, day.one = dates[1], span = ncol(rain))

# indices in periods of 7 days
rainfall(rain, day.one = dates[1], span = ncol(rain),
         timeseries = TRUE, intervals = 7)
```

Temperature indices take an array with maximum temperature in the first layer and minimum temperature in the second.

```r
dates = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-31")

tmax = get_chirts(lonlat, dates, var = "Tmax", product = "CHIRTS-ERA5",
                  as.matrix = TRUE)

tmin = get_chirts(lonlat, dates, var = "Tmin", product = "CHIRTS-ERA5",
                  as.matrix = TRUE)

temp = array(c(tmax, tmin), dim = c(dim(tmax), 2),
             dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(tmax), NULL))

temperature(temp, day.one = dates[1], span = ncol(tmax))

GDD(temp, day.one = dates[1], span = ncol(tmax), tbase = 10)
```

`precip_indices()` remains in **chirps** as a simple example of how to compute indices from a `chirps` data frame. Use climatrends for analysis.

## Raw raster products

The `*_raw()` functions return the CHC files as `SpatRaster` objects with one layer per day. Use them for large areas or custom workflows with **terra**.

```r
library("terra")

dates = c("2017-11-15", "2017-11-20")

v3 = get_chirps_raw(dates = dates, type = "sat")

tmax = get_chirts_era5_raw(dates = dates, var = "Tmax")

tx = get_chirts_raw(dates = c("2010-01-01", "2010-01-10"), var = "Tmax")
```

Once data are loaded as rasters, the **terra** functions apply.

```r
pts = vect(lonlat, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

rain = extract(v3, pts)

# crop to an area of interest
v3_crop = crop(v3, ext(-56, -54, -4, -2))

# total rainfall in the period
total = app(v3, sum)

# write to disk
writeRaster(v3, "chirps.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Servers

The CHC server is the default and the recommended source. `server = "ClimateSERV"` is kept for backward compatibility. It serves CHIRPS v2 only, which CHC retires after the December 2026 release, averaged over a small buffer around each point, and it is slow for more than a few points. ClimateSERV support for CHIRPS may be removed in a future release. `get_esi()` and `get_imerg()` still use ClimateSERV, as these products are not on the CHC server.

CHC blocks addresses that request many files that do not exist. **chirps** checks the first and last file of each request before reading the rest, and stops with a clear error when a file is missing. Keep requests within the period each product covers.

## Datasets citation

When using data obtained through this package, please cite the original datasets.

### CHIRPS v3
> Funk, C., Peterson, P., Harrison, L. et al. (2026). The Climate Hazards Center Infrared Precipitation with Stations, Version 3. Scientific Data, 13, 718. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-026-07096-4>

### CHIRTS-ERA5
> CHIRTS-ERA5 Data Repository https://doi.org/10.15780/G2F08J (2025). Data was accessed on [DATE].

### CHIRPS v2
> Funk C., Peterson P., Landsfeld M., … Michaelsen J. (2015). The climate hazards infrared precipitation with stations—a new environmental record for monitoring extremes. *Scientific Data*, 2, 150066. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2015.66>

### CHIRTS
> Verdin, A., Funk, C., Peterson, P., Landsfeld, M., Tuholske, C., and Grace, K. (2020). Development and validation of the CHIRTS-daily quasi-global high-resolution daily temperature data set. Scientific Data, 7, 303.
<https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-00643-7>
